texts.orig: The structures of two compounds of l -tartaric acid with quinoline, viz. the proton-transfer compound quinolinium hydrogen /C40._2 R ,3 R )-tartrate monohydrate, C9H8N +  C4H5O6 �  -H2O, /C40._I), and the anhydrous non-proton-transfer adduct with quinaldic acid, bis/C40._quinolinium-2-carboxylate) /C40._2 R ,3 R )-tartaric acid, 2C10H7NO2  C4H6O6, /C40._II), have been determined at 130 K. Compound /C40._I) has a three-dimensional honeycomb substructure formed from head-to-tail hydrogen-bonded hydrogen tartrate anions and water molecules. The stacks of  -bonded quinolinium cations are accommodated within the channels and are hydrogen bonded to it peripherally. Compound /C40._II) has a two-dimensional network structure based on pseudo-centrosymmetric head-to-tail hydrogenbonded cyclic dimers comprising zwitterionic quinaldic acid species which are interlinked by tartaric acid molecules.

texts.orig: Tartaric acid is a relatively strong diprotic chiral -hydroxy acid /C40._p Ka 1 = 2.93 and p Ka 2 = 4.23) and, therefore, is potentially capable of forming both 1:1 and 1:2 proton-transfer salts with most Lewis bases. However, with stoichiometric control it is possible to selectively form 1:1 hydrogen tartrates, and the crystal structures of a large number of these 1:1 salts have been reported, particularly since these compounds usually have good crystal morphology, allowing structure determination by single-crystal X-ray analysis, which is often not possible with the parent Lewis base. Applications have been with drugs such as epinephrine /C40._Carlstro È m, 1973), dextromoramide /C40._Bye, 1975), amosulalol /C40._Furuya et al. , 1989), alprenolol /C40._Gøo Â wka & Codding, 1989), phendimetrazine /C40._Glaser et al. , 1994) and tolterodine /C40._Kos Ïutic Â-Hulita & Z Ï egarac, 2005), as well as natural products such as alkaloids, e.g. strychnine /C40._Gould et al. , 1987), brucine /C40._Smith, Wermuth & White, 2006), quinine /C40._Ryttersgaard & Larsen, 2004), cinchonine /C40._Puliti et al. , 2001), cinchonidine /C40._Ryttersgaard & Larsen, 2003; Zhang et al. , 2003) and quincoridine /C40._Kania et al. , 2004), and amino acids, e.g. l -alanine /C40._Rajagopal et al. , 2002), l -proline /C40._Subha Nandhini et al. , 2001), d -, l - and dl -histidine /C40._Marchewska et al. , 2003; Rajagopal et al. , 2003; Johnson & Feeder, 2004 a , b , c ), and l -lysine /C40._Debrus et al. , 2005).
